html:
A long poem in Italian by Dante Alighieri, begun around 1308 and finished shortly before his death in 1321. In it Dante, lost in a dark wood at the age of 35 in the year 1300, travels through the three realms of the dead.

  • Inferno: Virgil, the Roman poet, leads him down through the nine circles of Hell, where sinners suffer punishments that fit their sins.
  • Purgatorio: they climb the mountain of Purgatory, where souls are cleansed.
  • Paradiso: Beatrice, the woman Dante loved, guides him up through the heavens to a vision of God.

It has 100 cantos in terza rima, a rhyme scheme Dante invented. It is full of real people: popes and Florentine politicians in Hell, and saints such as Thomas Aquinas and Francis of Assisi in Paradise. It sums up medieval theology, science and politics.

Written in Tuscan rather than Latin, it did more than any other book to make Tuscan the base of the Italian language. Boccaccio called it "divine", and the word was later added to its title.
